newsitem.title: USA: Four dead in Long Island plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Four dead in Long Island plane crash.

text.p: Four people were killed on Saturday when a single engine Piper Cherokee plane crashed in a vacant parking lot near Melville, Long Island about 50 miles east of midtown Manhattan, authorities said.
The plane reportedly burst into flames as it crashed in the lot and smashed into a warehouse about 9:13 p.m. (EDT), Stephen Peters, an FAA spokesman said.

"The four-seater took off from Bridgeport, Conn., and was cleared to land at Republic Airport in Farmingdale, L.I. The pilot exercised a missed approach and went one-and one-half miles northwest of the airport and crashed," he said.
Investigators from the National Transportation Safety Board will inspect the scene on Sunday to determine what caused the crash, he said.
"Visibility was very poor on Long Island all evening. It was foggy when the plane crashed," a Suffolk County Police Department spokesman said.
